sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer systems that understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of neural network called transformers and are trained on vast amounts of text to learn how language works.

sections.title: How Do LLMs Process Text?
sections.body: LLMs break down input text into smaller parts, like words or characters, which are then transformed into numerical representations called embeddings. These embeddings help the model understand the meaning and relationships between different words.

sections.title: The Importance of Prompts
sections.body: The way we ask questions or give instructions to LLMs, known as prompts, is very important. Even small changes in wording can lead to big differences in the answers we get, so crafting effective prompts is a key skill.

sections.title: Techniques to Improve LLM Performance
sections.body: There are special techniques, like Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, that help improve how LLMs respond. These methods guide the model to think step-by-step, which can lead to more accurate and reliable answers.

sections.title: Challenges and Solutions
sections.body: Despite their capabilities, LLMs can sometimes produce incorrect or misleading information, known as hallucinations. To address this, new prompting tools are being developed to refine user prompts and enhance the reliability of LLM responses, especially in educational settings.

turns.question: What role do embeddings play in Large Language Models?
turns.answer: They capture semantic relationships between tokens.
